title: Business term loans
metaDescription: Business term loans provide a lump sum repaid on a fixed schedule for planned one-time needs like expansion, equipment, or refinancing. Learn when a term loan commonly fits.
summary: The business term-loan page explains when a fixed-amount, scheduled-repayment loan can fit planned projects, growth investments, and certain refinancing needs.

hero.title: Business term loans for planned costs and growth projects.
hero.lead: A term loan is built for a specific need with a defined cost and repayment schedule. Use this page to understand when term financing commonly fits and when another structure may be more flexible.

quickAnswer.definition: is a fixed amount of capital borrowed up front and repaid on a set schedule over time. It is commonly used for one-time business needs such as expansion, equipment, refinancing, or a defined growth project.

whoItFitsHeading: A fixed amount for a defined need

whoItFits.heading: When a term loan tends to fit
items: A one-time project with a clear budget
Expansion or renovation with defined costs
Equipment or asset purchases that do not require a revolving facility

whenItMayNotFit.heading: When a term loan may not fit as well
items: Recurring cash-flow gaps may point more directly to a line of credit or another flexible working-capital structure.
Projects centered on owner-occupied real estate or SBA-specific goals may require comparing SBA 7(a) or SBA 504 first.

howFund44Fits.heading: How Fund44 fits

bullets: Separates planned one-time borrowing needs from revolving cash-flow products.
Connects term-loan research to the financing hub, line-of-credit comparison content, and the preview flow.

eligibilityCards.title: Repayment capacity
eligibilityCards.description: Lenders commonly review revenue, cash flow, and debt obligations to understand whether the business can support fixed payments.

eligibilityCards.title: Defined use of funds
eligibilityCards.description: A term loan is usually easier to size when the project, asset, or refinancing goal is clearly described.

eligibilityCards.title: Operating history
eligibilityCards.description: Time in business and recent operating performance often shape how a lender underwrites the request.

sectionDisclosureHtml: Fund44 is not a lender. Business term-loan eligibility, product availability, timelines, and terms are determined by third-party lenders and vary by provider and by business profile. This page is educational only.

ctaBanner.heading: Planning a one-time project or investment?
ctaBanner.subheading: Preview whether a term loan, an SBA path, or a more flexible option fits the need you are trying to fund.

commonQuestions.question: How does a business term loan work?
commonQuestions.answer: A term loan provides a lump sum up front and is repaid over time on a fixed schedule. That structure can work well when the amount needed and the business purpose are already defined.

commonQuestions.question: What is the difference between a term loan and a line of credit?
commonQuestions.answer: A term loan suits a one-time planned expense, while a line of credit is designed for ongoing or unpredictable borrowing needs. The right fit depends on whether you need a fixed amount once or ongoing access to capital.

commonQuestions.question: What documents may be needed for a term loan?
commonQuestions.answer: Common examples include business financials, bank statements, tax returns, and a clear use-of-funds summary. Exact requirements vary by lender and by the financing request.

commonQuestions.question: Does Fund44 issue business term loans?
commonQuestions.answer: No. Fund44 does not issue business term loans. Eligibility and terms are determined by third-party lenders.
